## Summary

Research confidence is **Moderate**. Some of this break's ideal conditions are confirmed by sources; others rest on limited evidence. It is the class the app computes from the evidence (how well the break's ideal conditions are documented), not a forecast and not a probability.

Main gaps:

- Sources disagree about the wave size this break works in.
- Sources disagree about the best tide.
- Limited information is available about the swell period this break needs.
- No survey, scientific or official source confirms the best swell direction.

| Variable | Research confidence | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Swell direction | Moderate | Supported by 6 independent sources, including a forecast site's spot guide. |
| Swell size | Low | Supported by 2 independent sources, including a community source; 2 disagree. |
| Swell period | Low | Supported by one source (a forecast site's spot guide). |
| Wind | Moderate | Supported by 4 independent sources, including a forecast site's spot guide. |
| Tide | Low | Supported by one source (a community source); 6 disagree. |
| Bottom / bathymetry | Moderate | Described by 3 independent sources, including a community source. |

| How the wave breaks | Moderate | Described by 5 independent sources, including a forecast site's spot guide. |

Research notes (research_evidence.json):

> Tide: the profile's 'mid' is contradicted. All tides is stated by Surf-Forecast, WannaSurf (falling best), both Macaronis Resort pages, Indonesian Surf Guide and Surf Indonesia, plus Surfer Today (unread); only Surfing-Waves.com says mid tide. Wind: NE (Surf-Forecast, 45 deg), E (Surf Indonesia, 90 deg) and E-SE (Indonesian Surf Guide and Surfing-Waves, 112.5 deg) all lie within 45 deg of the profile's 70; several sources stress that it handles most winds (WannaSurf lists six good directions, the resort says some prefer a light onshore SW breeze). The E-SE values are 42.5 deg off, close to the agreement limit. Swell direction: SW (Surf-Forecast, Surf Indonesia, Resort), S-SW with 200-210 deg best (Resort surf page, slightly south of the profile's 210-245 optimum), SW-W (Indonesian Surf Guide), W-SW-S (WannaSurf). Size: WannaSurf 3-5 ft start, holds 10 ft+; Resort 2-8 ft (3-6 ft ideal); Surfing-Waves 2-8 ft; Indonesian Surf Guide waist high to 1.5x overhead. All are consistent with 3-10 ft, though the resort and Surfing-Waves do not state a scale. Period: no numbers found. Season: May-October (Surf-Forecast), surfable almost daily in the southern winter (Resort), year-round (Surf Indonesia). The two resort pages are one publisher, the break's own resort operator. The Inertia page was dropped (claims not on it). Surfer Today still 403. No peer-reviewed or survey source found.

## Ideal conditions

Directions are compass degrees the swell or wind comes FROM, ranges clockwise. Heights keep the scale each source states (breaking face, Hawaiian, swell or relative to the surfer); the app's sizes are breaking face heights in feet. Sources are numbered as in [Sources](#sources).

### Swell height

| Field | Research value | Status | Sources | App model setting |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Minimum suitable | 2 ft [S4, S8] · 3–5 ft [S2] | conflicting | S2, S4, S8 | `wave_height_min_ft` 3 ft (breaking face) |
| Ideal range | 2–8 ft | documented | S6, S8 | no separate setting; working range 3–10 ft |
| Maximum suitable | 8 ft [S4] · 10 ft+ (open-ended) [S2] · 1.5x overhead [S6] | conflicting | S2, S3, S4, S6 | `wave_height_max_ft` 10 ft (breaking face) |

Notes:

- **Minimum suitable**: The resort and Surfing-Waves give 2 ft as the bottom of the range, while WannaSurf says it starts working at 1.0-1.5 m / 3-5 ft; none of the three says whether these are face or offshore swell heights.
  - S4 (Macaronis Resort): “Macas holds from 2 – 8 feet and technically doesn't get any bigger than this; it just becomes more hollow and round.”
  - S8 (Surfing-Waves.com): “from 2 foot to 8 foot”
  - S2 (WannaSurf): “Starts working at 1.0m-1.5m / 3ft-5ft and holds up to 3m+ / 10ft+”
- **Ideal range**: Surfing-Waves gives its best conditions as 2 to 8 ft (scale not stated); the Indonesian Surf Guide gives wave size as waist high to 1.5x overhead, a face height relative to the surfer that is not converted here.
  - S8 (Surfing-Waves.com): “from 2 foot to 8 foot”
  - S6 (Ultimate Indonesian Surf Guide (indonesiansurfguide.com)): “Wave size | Waist high to 1.5x overhead”
- **Maximum suitable**: The resort says it holds 2-8 ft and does not get bigger, only more hollow, WannaSurf says it holds up to 3 m+ / 10 ft+, and the Indonesian Surf Guide tops out at 1.5x overhead; Surfer Today (search summary, not read directly) says big groundswells make it dangerous.
  - S4 (Macaronis Resort): “Macas holds from 2 – 8 feet and technically doesn't get any bigger than this; it just becomes more hollow and round.”
  - S2 (WannaSurf): “Starts working at 1.0m-1.5m / 3ft-5ft and holds up to 3m+ / 10ft+”
  - S6 (Ultimate Indonesian Surf Guide (indonesiansurfguide.com)): “Wave size | Waist high to 1.5x overhead”
  - S3 (Surfer Today): “Big ground swells turn Macaronis into a dangerous, snarling beast of a wave”

### Swell direction

| Field | Research value | Status | Sources | App model setting |

| Ideal bearing | 225° (SW) | documented | S1, S4, S5, S6, S7 | `optimal_swell_direction` 210–245° (SSW to WSW, clockwise) |

Notes:

- **Ideal bearing**: Surf-Forecast, Surf Indonesia and the resort name southwest; the Indonesian Surf Guide widens it to SW-W, and the resort's surf page says any S-SW swell works and that 200-210 deg gives its best-known form, so SW (225) is the direction every source includes.
  - S1 (Surf-Forecast (surf-forecast.com)): “the ideal swell angle is from the southwest”
  - S4 (Macaronis Resort): “Generally a south west ground swell will cause Macaronis to break most mechanically”
  - S7 (Surf Indonesia (surfindonesia.com)): “Best swell direction: Macaronis: SW”
  - S6 (Ultimate Indonesian Surf Guide (indonesiansurfguide.com)): “Macaronis works on any tide, with a SW to W swell direction providing optimal lines.”
  - S5 (Macaronis Resort): “Macaronis works in any S-SW swell direction; it is more of a barrel during South swells, and with swells @ 200 – 210 degrees it gains its reputation”
- **Acceptable range**: WannaSurf lists W, SW and S as good swell directions (180-270 deg), and the resort's surf page says it works in any S-SW swell.
  - S2 (WannaSurf): “Good swell directionWest, SouthWest, South”
  - S5 (Macaronis Resort): “Macaronis works in any S-SW swell direction; it is more of a barrel during South swells, and with swells @ 200 – 210 degrees it gains its reputation”
- **Blocked directions**: No excerpt names blocked or shadowed directions.
- **Exposure**: Surf-Forecast calls it an exposed reef break, and Surfer Today (search summary, not read directly) says it is exposed to storm swells from the Southern Indian Ocean.
  - S3 (Surfer Today): “the spot is exposed to storm swells generated in the Southern Indian Ocean”
  - S1 (Surf-Forecast (surf-forecast.com)): “is an exposed reef break that has very reliable surf”

## Conflicting information

- **Swell height · minimum suitable**: The resort and Surfing-Waves give 2 ft as the bottom of the range, while WannaSurf says it starts working at 1.0-1.5 m / 3-5 ft; none of the three says whether these are face or offshore swell heights.
- **Swell height · maximum suitable**: The resort says it holds 2-8 ft and does not get bigger, only more hollow, WannaSurf says it holds up to 3 m+ / 10 ft+, and the Indonesian Surf Guide tops out at 1.5x overhead; Surfer Today (search summary, not read directly) says big groundswells make it dangerous.
- **Wind · offshore**: Surf-Forecast says offshore winds are from the northeast, Surf Indonesia says the best wind is east, and the Indonesian Surf Guide and Surfing-Waves say east to southeast.
- **Tide · preferred stage**: Surf-Forecast, WannaSurf, both resort pages, the Indonesian Surf Guide, Surf Indonesia and Surfer Today (search summary) say all tides; only Surfing-Waves says mid tide.
- **Seasonality · prime months**: Surf-Forecast favours May-October, the resort says it is surfable almost every day in the southern winter, and Surf Indonesia gives year-round as the best time.
